newsitem.title: USA: Duke sees Oconee nukes restarting in January.
newsitem.headline: Duke sees Oconee nukes restarting in January.

text.p: Duke Power Co's 2,538 megawatt (MW) Oconee nuclear power facility in Seneca, S.C. is likely to resume power production in January, 1997 after being shut due to an accident in September, a company spokesman said.
"At this point, we do plan to restart all three units (at Oconee) in January," spokesman Rick Zuercher said Monday.
The 846 MW Oconee unit 2 was shut Sept 24 after seven workers were scalded, four of them critically, when a steam pipe burst in the non-nuclear part of the unit.
Units 1 and 3, each also with a capacity of 846 MW, were subsequently shut for inspections to ensure the same steam pipe problems would not occur.

"We have done some extensive review, and we are in the process of modifying the piping system in the moisture separator reheater drain line that failed at Oconee 2, for all three units," Zuercher said.
Oconee unit 3 is also undergoing a scheduled autumn maintenance and refueling.
Duke Power has a total generation capacity of about 18,500 MW, of which the Oconee plant accounts for about 14 percent.
